staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the crash against this staged vulnerable checkout, and the line anchors below are grounded in this tree. The sample metadata names vulnerable commit `e5289e606c4b55b0fac29046c8343958248189e7`, but the prepared ARVO workspace is on the commit above; the staged `patch.diff` still edits the same vulnerable `flb_utils_write_str()` blocks present here.

evidence_note: Stage 02 used the staged `sample_info.json`, `patch.diff`, `sanitizer_trace.txt`, `default_crash_trace.txt`, `reproduction_report.json`, `trace_feedback.json`, the saved `poc`, and the staged vulnerable workspace under `_work/src`. A local static replay of the exact witness bytes identified the first parsed 15-entry MessagePack object and the exact crashing top-level key. `run_flags.json` keeps `runtime_disambiguation` false, so no instrumentation or reruns were performed.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42488098 (fluent-bit): Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 1 found by fuzz target flb-it-fuzz-msgpack_parse_fuzzer_OSSFUZZ [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42488098
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / trace_feedback.json / staged vulnerable source / staged poc bytes
bug_description.normalized: The staged 512-byte witness passes the harness `size == 512` gate, so `flb_msgpack_raw_to_json_sds()` computes `out_size = 768`, allocates one SDS with `alloc = 768`, and `msgpack_unpack_next()` parses the first 388 bytes as a 15-entry MessagePack map. When `flb_msgpack_to_json()` serializes that root object with logical payload limit `left = 767`, the crashing `MSGPACK_OBJECT_STR` at `msgpack2json:528` is the top-level map key at index 9 (the 10th pair) with raw bytes `e0e0e000012a0200a50200a5888888f288888800`. `msgpack2json()` has already emitted that key's opening quote at output offset 723, so `flb_utils_write_str()` enters the same call with `*off = 724` and `available = 43`. In that call, control-byte escapes for bytes 3/4/6/7/9/10 plus the literal `'*'` move the cursor to 761 and `written` to 37. On the staged x86_64 clang build there is no staged `-funsigned-char` override, so `uint32_t c = (uint32_t) str[i];` sign-extends byte 15 `0xf2` to `0xfffffff2` and the valid UTF-8 sequence `f2 88 88 88` enters the `c > 0xFFFF` branch. `flb_utf8_decode()` still produces `codepoint = 0x88208`, and the vulnerable line-710 `snprintf(..., "\\u%04x", codepoint)` checks only for 6 bytes beforehand but returns `len = 7` for `\\u88208`, so copying that escape moves `p` to 768 and makes `written = 44 > available = 43`. The later `available - written` guard is a `size_t` subtraction, so it wraps instead of rejecting the trailing byte 19 `0x00`; the control-byte branch at `flb_utils_write_str:650` then starts a 6-byte `\\u0000` copy at offset 768, and its second byte is the first write at offset 769 outside the 769-byte SDS user area inside ASan's 785-byte allocation. The fix adds `if ((available - written) < len) return FLB_FALSE;` after each escape `snprintf`, preventing the overlong `\\u88208` copy and the wrapped line-650 control escape that follows it.

source.description: First project statement on the vulnerable path that consumes attacker-controlled input and creates the initial JSON output budget from it.
source.value_from: The staged witness has sha256 `d3e8f165bab403043f6787e79001a2ddebac6dfd5ef113ce4c7dd58d1c78bc23` and the harness only calls this path when `size == 512`. This statement therefore materializes `out_size = 768`, which becomes the vulnerable buffer extent later walked by the crashing serializer.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. On the exact crashing key, byte 15 `0xf2` reaches `const char *str` without unsigned normalization, so `uint32_t c = (uint32_t) str[i];` sign-extends it to `0xfffffff2` and the call takes the `c > 0xFFFF` branch. `flb_utf8_decode()` still resolves bytes `f2 88 88 88` to `0x88208`, so this `snprintf` returns 7 for `\\u88208` after only a 6-byte availability check. The patch adds `if ((available - written) < len) return FLB_FALSE;` immediately after this line and duplicates the same obligation at the sibling `\\u%.4x` and `\\u%.4hhx` escape sites.

sink.description: Closest project sink to the ASan crash. The final control-byte escape copy executes after the remaining-space arithmetic has wrapped, so the `\\u0000` write starts at the last in-bounds byte and immediately continues past the end of the original SDS allocation.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports the top frame in `encoded_to_buf` at `src/flb_utils.c:577`, but the callsite that decides to perform the overflowing copy is this line in `flb_utils_write_str()`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The raw fuzzer buffer and its length enter project code here. `in_size` defines the initial SDS budget, and `in_buf` is later parsed into the MessagePack object tree whose exact top-level key bytes reach the crashing escape path.

parser_admitted.description: At this point `msgpack_unpack_next()` has already accepted the witness's first MessagePack object and project code has entered the JSON-conversion path that later reaches `flb_utils_write_str()`.

fine_trace.note: Source. The harness admits only the exact 512-byte witness, so this first project-side use of attacker-controlled input materializes `out_size = 768` as the initial JSON buffer budget for the vulnerable conversion path.

The derived budget is allocated as one SDS string. `flb_sds_create_size(768)` yields `alloc = 768` plus one terminator byte; together with the SDS header this is the 785-byte heap region named by ASan, and all later serializer writes target this same `out_buf`.

The same raw buffer is parsed into the first MessagePack object that `msgpack2json()` will walk. A static replay of the saved bytes shows this call consumes the first 388 bytes as a 15-entry map, and that its top-level map key at index 9 has raw bytes `e0e0e000012a0200a50200a5888888f288888800`.

The serializer enters `msgpack2json()` with logical payload limit `left = json_size - 1 = 767` on the SDS from step 2. The saved stack frame at `msgpack2json:616` shows the later crash occurs while this root map is being walked under that shared `off` and `left` budget.

At frame `msgpack2json:528`, the exact crashing `MSGPACK_OBJECT_STR` is the top-level root-map key at index 9 (10th pair) with bytes `e0e0e000012a0200a50200a5888888f288888800`. `msgpack2json()` has just emitted that key's opening quote at output offset 723, so `flb_utils_write_str()` receives this key with `*off = 724`, `size = left = 767`, and `available = 43`.

fine_trace.code: len = snprintf(tmp, sizeof(tmp) - 1, "\\u%.4hhx", (unsigned char) c);\nencoded_to_buf(p, tmp, len);\np += len;
fine_trace.note: In the same call, bytes 0-2 and 8/11-14 are skipped as invalid UTF-8 without advancing `p`; control bytes 3/4/6/7/9/10 take this branch and the intervening byte 5 `'*'` stays literal. Those transformations move the cursor from 724 to 761 and raise `written` from 0 to 37 before the later UTF-8 escape is attempted.

Root cause. Still in the same key call, byte 15 `0xf2` reaches `uint32_t c = (uint32_t) str[i];` through plain `char`, so on the staged build it sign-extends to `0xfffffff2` and enters the `c > 0xFFFF` branch. `flb_utf8_len()` still reads bytes 15-18 `f2 88 88 88` as one 4-byte UTF-8 sequence and `flb_utf8_decode()` resolves `codepoint = 0x88208`. The guard immediately above only checked `(available - written) < 6`, which passes because step 6 left exactly 6 bytes, but this `snprintf` returns `len = 7` for `\\u88208`.
The unchecked Unicode escape from step 7 copies 7 bytes at output offsets 761 through 767 and leaves `p = 768`, one byte farther than the six-byte check budget allowed.

After step 8, `written` becomes 44 while the call's `available` from step 5 remained 43. The next guard reuses `available - written` as a `size_t`, so the subtraction wraps instead of going negative and no longer blocks later escapes in this same `flb_utils_write_str()` invocation.

Sink. The trailing key byte 19 `0x00` re-enters the control-byte branch at line 649 after step 9 wrapped the remaining-space arithmetic. `encoded_to_buf()` starts the 6-byte `\\u0000` copy at output offset 768; the first byte uses the last in-bounds terminator slot and the second byte lands at offset 769, matching ASan's first out-of-bounds write in `encoded_to_buf:577`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes at buffer level: the missing post-`snprintf` length check acts on the same `out_buf` and cursor budget whose original allocation appears at `flb_msgpack_raw_to_json_sds:671`.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. Static replay of the exact witness identifies frame `msgpack2json:528` as serialization of the top-level root-map key at index 9 (`e0e0e000012a0200a50200a5888888f288888800`), reached from the enclosing map walker at `msgpack2json:616`; within that same `flb_utils_write_str()` call, signed promotion of byte `0xf2` selects the line-710 `\\u%04x` branch, the overlong `\\u88208` copy advances the cursor to 768, and the trailing `0x00` then hits the saved sink `flb_utils_write_str:650 -> encoded_to_buf:577`.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The exact top-level key bytes `e0e0e000012a0200a50200a5888888f288888800` from the saved witness supply both the control bytes and the valid `f2 88 88 88` UTF-8 sequence whose leading byte is sign-extended into the `c > 0xFFFF` branch, driving the same `flb_utils_write_str()` call from `msgpack2json:528` through the overlong escape to the final line-650 overflow.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42488098 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, fed the staged `poc` to `/out/flb-it-fuzz-msgpack_parse_fuzzer_OSSFUZZ`, and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` in `encoded_to_buf -> flb_utils_write_str -> msgpack2json`.

format.name: 512-byte raw input for `flb-it-fuzz-msgpack_parse_fuzzer_OSSFUZZ`
format.contract: Exactly the staged 512-byte witness `poc` with sha256 `d3e8f165bab403043f6787e79001a2ddebac6dfd5ef113ce4c7dd58d1c78bc23`. The harness rejects all other sizes. Static replay of this exact witness parses a 15-entry root map whose top-level key at index 9 is `e0e0e000012a0200a50200a5888888f288888800`; when serialized, that same key reaches `flb_utils_write_str()` with `*off = 724`, expands control bytes to offset 761, enters the sign-extended line-710 `\\u%04x` branch for bytes `f2 88 88 88`, emits the overlong `\\u88208` escape, and then overflows on the key's trailing `0x00`. The staged evidence grounds this exact witness and this exact parsed-key layout only; it does not prove a broader class of MessagePack inputs.
